transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. What brings you to see me today?

Well, I came in because things have really fallen apart for me lately. Ever since my wife’s fall, I’ve gone from being the man who always had the lists and the plan to... well, just sitting at the kitchen table staring at her medication chart. 

I find myself crying, or snapping at people over absolutely nothing. And I'm letting everything else pile up—the bills, my mentoring calls, even just basic housework. It’s like I just can’t make myself function anymore, and I need to figure out how to get back on track.
How long ago did your wife's fall happen?
It was about two months ago. Yeah, right around two months. That's when she fell, and... well, that's when everything at home just completely changed for us.
Do you find yourself having unwanted, intrusive memories or nightmares about the moment she fell?

No, not really. I don't have nightmares about the fall itself. And I'm not having... you know, sudden memories popping up of that specific moment. It's not the actual event that's the problem for me, it's just the reality of everything we have to deal with now.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in the hobbies and activities you used to enjoy?

No, I wouldn't say I've lost interest. I still care about the things I normally do. Like I mentioned with my mentoring... I still want to do it, and I know I'd enjoy it if I did. 

It's just that, with everything going on right now, I can't seem to focus or get myself organized enough to actually participate in any of it. But the interest itself hasn't gone away.
Before your wife's fall, were you experiencing any of these feelings of sadness, worry, or difficulty coping?

No, I wasn't. Before all this happened, I was doing fine. My wife's fall was only about two months ago, and... well, I only really started falling apart after the caregiving routine took over. It definitely wasn't an issue before that.
